And that was provocation of sorts. So that's why he came. And I happened to be outside in the yard at that moment, so he addressed me, too, and said, "Oh, hello, ma'am. How come you are here? How come you're not working anywhere, fulfilling your work obligation?" So I tried to explain, saying that I had small children and I was relieved from such work. But he continued in a different vein, saying something like, "Well, you know, there are easier jobs than that. You should go and report to the Tekstilac factory, and they would give you suitable work obligation. You should do so tomorrow." And while this conversation was going on, he noticed that the door of the garage behind the house was closed, so he said, "What's in the garage, by the way?" I didn't say anything to that. I just opened the door of the garage. And inside was our private car, Zastava 101, and some other things that we usually stored in the garage, mainly, two machining tools, lathes, that my husband used to do jobs on the side. And when he was leaving, he said, "Please don't let anyone come in here or take anything away. I'll come back." After that, the soldier left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Stojan Blagojevic before he turned up in your yard on the 27th of June?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Stojan Blagojevic, but my neighbour explained later that he used to work together with her husband in the Mebos company, where my husband had been employed as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So your neighbour could identify the soldier. Did you know who he was there -- you said he was in the military. Do you know whether he was working for the JNA or the 4th Detachment or any other body?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dressed in a military camouflage uniform. I can't recall whether the insignia on the uniform was of the JNA or of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So he told you that you should report to the textile factory the next day. Did you in fact report to the textile factory, or did you take some other action based on those instructions?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation took place in the afternoon, and several hours later, this soldier would come back later, with company, to officially confiscate the car. And around 6.00 or 7.00 p.m., from the neighbouring courtyard, Miroslav Tadic showed up. I knew that he was involved with the Red Cross, and I asked him to come up to the -- to my fence. It was just a few steps away. I wanted to talk to him and to explain what had just happened earlier that day. He told me that since I had small children, I didn't have to go and perform any work obligation, but he was not really authorised to decide, and he said that Simo Zaric would come instead and make an official protocol and implement the orders accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just clarify. This discussion you had with Miroslav Tadic, it took place after your car had been confiscated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I will come back to address the confiscation of your car, but for the moment, I'd just like to get the full details about your call to the textile factory. So you've testified that Mr. Simo Zaric would come and give you an official protocol and implement the orders accordingly. Did Mr. Zaric in fact call to you later that night?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic -- or Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The translation was not accurate. I don't believe that this was what the witness stated, that -- according to her testimony, what I understood in our language was that Mr. Tadic informed her that Simo Zaric would come and make some sort of information -- of some official information about the event that happened, and not that he will issue an order to her for this kind of labour. So maybe my colleagues from the Prosecutor could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Reidy, you can go back to that point and find out exactly what the conversation was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, I think you've gathered there's maybe a translation confusion. We're talking now about the conversation with Mr. Tadic that evening. And he told you that Mr. Simo Zaric would come back instead of him. What exactly was it that he said Mr. Zaric would do when he came by?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that Simo Zaric would take over, that he would explain to Simo Zaric the entire situation, and that he would then take over and help resolve the matter. He said that he personally was not in a position to decide.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think that explains it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just only one thing for the record. She said that "he will make a record of the event," this is something that we heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'll ask that specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Reidy, you can ask that again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We said "protocol" in order to denote some sort of official minutes or record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's an explanation from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Mrs. Delic, we have an interpreter's explanation of the matter. So could you now tell us if Mr. Zaric did in fact come by and, if so, what he did when he came to see you.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening hour, Mr. Zaric did indeed arrive, and I repeated my explanation about what had happened earlier that day. He said he would take care of it and that I didn't have to go to the Tekstilac factory the next day and that I didn't have to work because I had small children at home with me. That was the end of our conversation, and I had no further contact with Mr. Simo Zaric. And I should also note that this Stojan Blagojevic never came to my door again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric simply come and tell you that there was no need for you to turn up at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, the witness has clearly explained. So you can ask her whether there was anything else that he said. Instead of you repeating what she has already said, and you know, we are taking a bit too much time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: My question was: Did he give you anything in writing, or was all his information to you oral?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive anything in writing, no decision or anything like that. But he emphasised verbally that there should be no more problems, that he would take care of everything, and that I didn't have to go to perform any work obligation. I know that he made some notes in his pad, but I don't know what he wrote down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. What about the car that was taken away? Did you try to -- want to get it back?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, would bit of assistance -- there is some detailed information with respect to the confiscation of the car and indeed a document -- an exhibit that we would like to tender into evidence. So I'd now like to return to that. I just wanted to close the matter of -- her instructions to return to the textile factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: No. Because she didn't talk about the car at all. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'll move back to that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I mean, cars are important to some people.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely. And I'll turn to that right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You said that someone came back and confiscated the car. Could you tell us what happened when someone -- what happened with the car.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That soldier named Stojan Blagojevic -- at least, I learned later that was his name from several persons -- he said that he would be back shortly. And by "shortly," I mean an hour, not more. And he came back together with another soldier, whose name I also learned later. And they came carrying a written document which said that the car is being taken away to meet to all requirements of the Republika Srpska. It was signed by the Crisis Staff, and had the signature of Dr. Blagoje Simic on it. In the bottom right-hand corner, there was also a stamp next to the signature with the four letter "S" sign, and around the edge of the stamp, it said, "Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac," and also, "The Pelagicevo municipality in the process of being established."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender into evidence the document which the witness has -- is talking about. I have given copies to my colleagues. I've got copies here for the Bench and, of course, the registry. And I also have the original which the witness brought with her, if the Bench would like to instruct it, or perhaps the original could be placed -- or a copy could be placed on the ELMO for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How -- what is the title of the document? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The title is a "requisition order, dated the 27th of June, 1992, reference number 12/06/92."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask, could I -- I wish to produce and to enter into evidence a copy of the document. And the original is simply available for inspection, if that's okay with the Chamber. I'd rather give it back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can inspect the original. The Defence counsels can also inspect the original, just to make sure that the copies -- we will retain exact copies of the original. It's translated, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is a final revised English translation accompanying the document. Maybe could I ask for the number of the exhibit to be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number -- oh, first let me ask the Defence whether that have any objection to it being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first I would like to have a short look on the original, if I may, because it's -- well, this is a new document for us. But still, we can resolve this matter about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When was the document given to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. For the record, this document was disclosed originally to the first defendants who came in, I believe, August 1999 with the statements. Mr. Pantelic had a copy of it then. He then received it as volume 8 of his disclosure when he was acting as counsel for Blagoje Simic. Then, last week, I reproduced another copy of it with the draft translation for him, putting him on notice that I would be introducing it through this witness. I then gave him a final copy yesterday. And yesterday, I brought in the original. I left it for inspection. He looked at it, said, "I don't think it's important for my client," and gave it back to me. So he has -- and it's exactly the one he's looking at now. So this is not new. And he has also had an opportunity to inspect the original prior to this witness ever taking the stand. Sorry, just for the record, this document is referred to both in the statement of this witness, which Mr. Pantelic has had, and it's referred to in the statement of her husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I appreciate, of course, this very detailed explanation from my learned friends. In fact, I didn't say that this document was never tendered to us. But simply, as I said, I would just like to have a short look on the original. That's all, very simple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. You did say, "It's a new document for us." It's there on the transcript. And I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I do apologise myself. It's -- it was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- the meaning of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's wrong to mislead the Court, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, it was not the -- in that sense, of course. What I meant is that it's a new document for us to see in the original form. That was my --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But Ms. Reidy has explained that she had shown you the original before today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At this moment, I can confirm that this document has the -- has the title, also has the headings of the authority who issued this document. Of course, there is a stamp, there is a seal -- there is a seal, which it seems it's original. But -- I mean, these are all elements for one document to be, I would say, genuine. But I take a note -- and I have -- I got certain confrontations with my client. The signature is absolutely -- is not a signature of Dr. Blagoje Simic. In addition --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, Mr. Pantelic is now giving evidence. That's fine if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- he wants to put his client's case -- yeah, when Mr. Simic takes the stand, if that's what his wish is, we can hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, but just another detail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So your stand is that the signature is not that of your client. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, and also, Your Honour, there is, on the official transcript, you may see before the -- Dr. Blagoje Simic, in parentheses, there is a question mark, and then "for," which means that - according to my knowledge - I completely agree with the translator that someone probably signed for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, we -- yeah, we are dealing with admissibility only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So as to how much weight, you can deal with that in your Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course. And I can -- I don't have any objection for this document to be admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Your Honour, may I just say a few words?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to object to the admission of this document for formal reasons. As my colleague from the Prosecution said, this document has indeed been disclosed to us in the pre-trial stage, and we got it together with the documentation related to this witness. In the reciprocal procedure, we received this document. But in the pre-trial brief, the Prosecutor did not indicate this document would be used as evidence at the trial. It is an identical situation as with the book of Mr. Tihic which was disclosed to us, but the Prosecutor did not indicate in their trial brief that they will be introducing it. And then the Trial Chamber decided that it cannot be tendered. It's the same grounds in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... For these words of my colleague. In that case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you have agreed for your client. The record is that for Mr. Tadic, I think, there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the basis is not valid. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We concur with Mr. Lukic's objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was expecting that, actually. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of principle, also the Defence of Zaric agrees fully with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The objections are noted, but the Trial Chamber will go ahead and admit the document. Matters of weight can be discussed and resorted to by the Defence in their case. And at the end of the trial, the Trial Chamber will decide how much weight to attach to the document. So can we have the number, please, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's Exhibit P49 ter for the B/C/S version, and P49 for the English translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, just one minute. Mr. Pantelic, I -- as I understand your position, your position is that this document was issued for -- purports to be issued for and on behalf of Dr. Blagoje Simic but not by him. So it is signed by somebody who is signing that document as the issuant for and on behalf of Dr. Blagoje Simic. That's your stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. That is my submission. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I also ask -- I noted that there is a -- it's P49, which is on the ELMO. And it may be helpful to have P49 ter on the ELMO so that the accused can also see the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, again. Could we come down lower to the signature again a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, what is on the ELMO now is the photocopy -- the same one that everybody now has in front of them. The original is just in front of the witness. So just in case you thought that on the ELMO you were actually viewing the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like to see the original on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. Show it to Mr. Pantelic, please. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You will see on the translation a slash at the bottom against the signature, a slash, a question mark, and the word "for."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. And you confirm that that's what appears in the B/C/S version: the slash, the question mark, and "for,"" and then another slash?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, is for this particular detail is that that was some kind of intervention of the Translation Unit saying that they are not sure whether it is a word in B/C/S language "for." It is a usual approach in many of the documents that someone is making this detail. And that's my understanding. I mean, it is not actually the situation that we have in B/C/S version of document "slash," "question mark," "for," and then "slash." It is not the case. But rather, I think that it's a kind of -- maybe an opinion of the interpreter that that means that, this small blue detail in front of the title of Mr. Blagoje Simic, which means that it's for him and that someone is signing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: That's all right. No. I just want to know if in the B/C/S it just says "for." Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It seems to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: "For."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: "For."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And there's nothing else -- leave the question mark aside, the interpreter's question mark or someone else's question mark there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is no -- on the B/C/S version of document, there is no question mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And there is no slash, too. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is no slash, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just "for."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just "for."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You're welcome, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I just say that Mr. Pantelic is absolutely entitled to assume that the squiggle in the Cyrillic version could mean "for." And my understanding of the translation -- the English revised translation, is that the interpreter said, well, it could possibly mean it. But with respect, I think if you look at the squiggle which is beside the Cyrillic "DR," standing for Dr., it could be that. I'm not saying Mr. Pantelic's interpretation is completely wrong. But I don't think that necessarily means that that is "for."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. No. Ms. Reidy, this is your case. You are the people who got this document. So from your source, you should have been told what this is all about. You should have anticipated that there would be, you know, problems with the signature or anything, like it is usual in every document. So you should tell the Trial Chamber what the position of the Prosecution is.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position of the Prosecution is clear. It's going to come through this witness that she received this document. What was on it, I was simply -- I'm sorry, I didn't -- just trying to draw a distinction between Mr. Pantelic saying that that's what it is and that's what his impression of it is. And I just hope that's clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. All you have to say is, as far as the Prosecution case is concerned, this signature or this document, whatever it is, is this. That's all. You don't have to explain anything. Just tell the Trial Chamber what the position of the Prosecution about this is. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we go by the -- by the translation -- by the translators here that it possibly could mean "for." We have not spoken with Mr. Blagoje Simic. We cannot verify that he signed this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think that's what I meant. Just go ahead with your witness. Maybe it will become clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But the Prosecution's position is that the little squiggle is as the interpreters have made it clear on the English translation. It could possibly mean "for," but it is unclear as to whether that means it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, could you please have a look at the document that appears on the screen in front of you, and it's also to your right. And is this the document you were handed by Mr. Blagojevic when he came to confiscate your car?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's the document. I have been in possession of this document from that day, the 27th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. When -- I'd ask you to look at that document and to look to the third set of lines which need to be filled in, and there's some handwriting in it. And my understanding of the document is it says it's for the needs of the Bosanski Samac Crisis Staff. Was that your understanding at the time? Or you also said you thought it might be used for the army. What were you told when you were given this document?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't given any particular explanation, and I tried to find out from this document what will happen with my car, who will take it over.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The document says that at the time of requisitioning the items, a record should be compiled and signed by the owner and the user." Did that occur when you car was confiscated?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it -- it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to sign any document?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is it correct that the actual owner of the car is the name stated on that document, your husband Dragan Delic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The car was handed over with the car's documents which were in the car, as well as all the other documents that go together with the car, as well as two sets of keys. But this wasn't noted in any particular record or report.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The document says that: "Where an asset is requisitioned in the absence of the owner, it shall be done by a committee comprising three members." How many people came to requisition your husband's car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The committee would not come down. That would be just a legal owner, isn't it -- "If the asset is requisitioned in the absence of the owner, the requisition will be conducted by a committee comprising three members." Could that mean that the requisition is signed by the committee?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid I've got: "The requisition shall be conducted," not "the requisition order shall be issued by." So that's just -- I'm just following my logical interpretation of the word "conducted," rather than "requisition order issued by."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many people came to requisition your car? Was it Mr. Blagojevic by himself or was he in the company of anybody else?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besides Blagojevic, there was another soldier. He appeared later with another person. He didn't tell me the name. He didn't introduce himself. But I found out later that his name was Aco Jokic -- Joksic -- but I didn't know this person and I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever see your car after it was taken away by Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about ten days, I saw that my car was being driven around town by some person. I didn't see that the person who was driving the car was in a military uniform or any kind of uniform. I simply don't know who it was who was driving the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And was that the only time you saw your car for the rest of the time you remained in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Have you made any attempt to get back your car since you left Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And it states at the end, in any case, that with proper documentation -- I don't have any -- I don't have any papers any longer proving that I had the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether -- I think, sorry --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm now finished with my use of the documents, so maybe it can be taken from the ELMO, unless the Bench have any questions about the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I just have one question. She did say she didn't sign anything. Was there a copy of this order, was any copy given to her, just as a record that they had taken the car?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour was asking was this -- this document was given to you. Was this the only record given to you when your car was taken away?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only document that I have about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And just, what was the value of your car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not really very good at determining the value, but it states the make of the car is Zastava Stojadin 101. It wasn't new. It was perhaps five years old. So perhaps an estimate can be made later. But I'm not very good at giving you such an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I just have one question as well. In the English version, the third line in the first paragraph says inter alia: "The following shall be requisitioned for temporary-permanent use." Okay? And then the bottom paragraph only talks about reimbursement for the temporary use of assets or requisitioned goods and so on. I'm wondering what "temporary/permanent use" is. If the requisition was for permanent use and not temporary use of the car, then the bottom paragraph would seem to indicate that the Crisis Staff was not going to be giving any composition, even with proper documentation. And whether it's clarification from counsel or from the witness as to the meaning of "temporary/permanent use," I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. I think maybe the witness would certainly be in a better position than me to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But were you told whether your car was just being temporarily requisitioned or permanently requisitioned? Any indication as to what exactly it was being used for or how long it would be kept?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The car was taken without any additional explanations. And in such situations, a visit by these two soldiers was sufficient for me just to feel happy that they left as soon as they could, and I wasn't even thinking about the material value of the goods that were being taken away. I didn't receive any kind of explanation about this, neither did I seek any explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It may not be of assistance, but I think that's as far as we can go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Well, I think that's as best as one can. And I'm assuming that you're also going to be discussing perhaps whether the two lathe machinery items were also removed or left in the garage, as the case might be.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, I will -- I was going to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No problem. But is the Bench satisfied with the inquiries about the document itself, while I ask the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Delic --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, I can give the original back to the witness, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, you've testified and shown us a document showing that your car was taken. Was there other items from your garage, such as the machinery, or other things taken, or from your house?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, nothing more was taken. But it was indicated to me by this soldier, Blagojevic, that I shouldn't touch anything and that he would come back to look for these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he come back?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never came back. It all remained in the garage after the 4th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have any foodstuffs in the garage at the time?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was just a crate of beer there. And they took that away, of course, without making any kind of record. On that day, the 27th of June, I know that it was very difficult to get those kinds of beverages on the market, so they took that, thinking that I probably obtained that from somewhere. So they were questioning me about it. But they were very satisfied to have found these drinks. They didn't take anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know whether any other cars or vehicles were taken from any of your other non-Serb neighbours?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the vehicles had already been confiscated. So it was quite strange to find a car like that in a garage after such a long time. And the reaction was such that -- that even this confiscation was carried out very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you notice whether your Serb neighbours were -- still had their cars, were driving around in their cars?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they had their own cars and used them for their private purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, I apologise if you might be going to ask this. But once again, just in case, could you clarify with the witness whether she went and spoke to anybody in official circles in the municipality about the confiscation. You know, maybe just a "yes "or a "no," and if "no," why not?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I don't think I need to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk with anybody from the official authorities. During those days -- and it should be clear -- that it was very difficult for me to live in such conditions and that something like that never even crossed my mind, to ask for my vehicle or to ask for an explanation why it was confiscated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: The reason I was asking the question was because in the circumstances of the work obligation in the textile factory, of course you did have a few words first of all with Mr. Tadic, and then Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. secondly, with Mr. Zaric, who helped you. And -- so therefore, I was wondering whether, with respect to the property, you might have done the same thing, spoken to somebody like Mr. Tadic -- like Mr. Zaric, for example, or somebody else. But I mean, you've answered the question. But to explain why I was asking it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In fact, I will re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I understand you said it was in the conditions, you didn't think of going to an official authority. But you did speak with Mr. Tadic a number of hours later. Did you mention it to him that your car had been taken at that time?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that in that conversation, but this was considered to be normal in these conditions. And as he explained, he said, "This is normal right now, in this situation."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So you told him your car had been taken, and he said that was normal.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever ask him why your car was taken and why some of your Serb neighbours' cars weren't taken? Was that normal?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have that much courage to ask why the vehicles hadn't been confiscated from them. I didn't ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You said that you spoke with Mr. Zaric later. Did you also refer to the incident of your car being confiscated in your conversations with him?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I mentioned that topic later. I was satisfied just about the fact that he would try to do something so that I would not be called for work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have further conversation -- you testified about one conversation with Mr. Tadic in your yard on that day. Did you have further conversations with Mr. Tadic after the 27th of June and before you left Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first contact, when I complained to him that I was afraid that something like that would happen again. And he himself confirmed that it could happen, that somebody could come to the house and take something and that -- then I talked about the possibility of leaving the town as well as whether it was possible that I be included in the list for exchange. So I was asking about the possibility of getting out of the town in some way. The town at that time was closed. It was like a town camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And why did you ask Mr. Tadic about the possibilities of leaving the town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was involved in work in the Serbian Red Cross, and he dealt with exchange issues and the possibility of leaving town.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how did you come to know that it was Mr. Tadic who you should deal with if you wanted to leave town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that because certain similar exchanges had already taken place. When I say "similar," what I mean are exchanges through which citizens left. They had the opportunity or the possibility to leave Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why did you want to leave Samac? Why did you raise the question of getting out of Samac with Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was already obvious that there was no other way to normalise the life of my children, my husband, and myself, in that town. I couldn't just get into my own vehicle and leave town when I wanted to. My husband was arrested, and the conditions that he was there and all the things that he had to bear there were getting worse and worse. So I spent many hours, a lot of time, trying to get my name and my husband's name on some list for exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to deal with that in greater detail. But could I ask you first if you also know someone by the name of Ilija Ristic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could I just interrupt before you do that. I don't see, unless my eyes are deceiving me, an answer to your question on page 66, line 24 and 25, when you say, Ms. Reidy, "Why didn't you raise the question of getting out of Samac with Mr. Tadic?" If you can point to me to the answer, fine. But I don't -- I don't think I heard it, and I don't think I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think it's because I badly phrased the question. Is your concern why she raised it with Mr. Tadic specifically, or what was her impulse for deciding -- for raising the topic of leaving at all? Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: With Mr. Tadic specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. I thought I had covered that in previous questions, but I have no problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: If the answer is simply because he was involved with the Red Cross, fine. If not, maybe there's more. I -- you know, I leave it up to you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think it would be helpful just for the record if you could clarify why was it again, with Mr. Tadic that you raised the possibility of leaving Samac.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely because he dealt with exchanges. He was involved in the work of the Serbian Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd asked you whether or not you know anybody called Ilija Ristic.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him as a citizen of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Ilija Ristic in Bosanski Samac after the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During a visit to the Red Cross, on the premises of the Red Cross somewhere, I met him in the corridor. I don't know what day it was. When he saw me, he asked me right away what I wanted and why did I come there. Then I told him, "Because I wanted to ask to have my name and my children's names placed on the exchange list." He was surprised, in a way, and he said, "Well, I thought that you would remain as loyal citizens here in town. And now you are asking to leave."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you say back to him?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I don't have any other means of living a normal life. I don't have any other funds. And this is the only way for me to get out of this situation that I am in."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've testified to trying to get your name and your children's name on a list. How did you do this? You met with Mr. Tadic on the 27th of June, and then what efforts were involved in trying to get your name and your children's name on a list for exchange?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I had at that moment was as follows: Just the fact that I reported in there meant that I consented to some -- to this particular way of leaving town, because that was the only way that was open to me. In my first contacts, it was explained to me that for me, because I was a Croat, and for my children, there would be no problem to do something like that but that my husband was problematic because it wouldn't be so easy for him to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And your husband was problematic why?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never got a specific official explanation why he was a problem. But when speaking to Mr. Tadic, I always got the same answer, that it was very difficult and that all matters related to prisoners were decided by the Crisis Staff, which was based in Pelagicevo. However, I never got any official information about that. I always associated permissions for certain people to be released with the name of Stevan Todorovic, although I don't know what his capacity for official decision-making was and what his true influence was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You said that you reported -- the fact that you'd reported to that place meant that you had given some form of consent. Where exactly were you reporting?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always went to the offices of the Serbian Red Cross, where I could find Mr. Tadic, who was the person to address on such matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many -- could you tell us to the best of your knowledge roughly how many times you went to the Red Cross or spoke with Mr. Tadic about an exchange between the 27th of June and the 4th of September?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many times I went there, but it must have been at least four or five times.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you went, were you given any information as to what the exchange would involve, what you'd be allowed to bring with you, that sort of information?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only sometime in August that the possibility of such an exchange began to materialise and that it became possible even for my husband, perhaps, to be included in such a list. I was told that I could take some personal belongings and not more than 200 Deutschmark.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who told you that information?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When did you find out that you were actually going to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After several attempts, I was officially informed on the 3rd of September, the evening of the 3rd of September, by a messenger carrying a piece of paper with a list of names on it. I was not allowed to inspect this paper and read the names. I was just told by this messenger that I should be ready for the exchange that was scheduled for 8.00 in the morning. In fact, at 8.00 in the morning, we were supposed to show up -- to report to the courtyard of the school where buses or trucks would be waiting and that one travel bag per person was allowed as luggage.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you know the messenger who came to your door?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him. His name -- or nickname was Pasan; his last name was Subasic. And working as a messenger was his work duty or work obligation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, prior to being told - this was in September - you also said that in September there had been another attempt to arrest you. Was this before or after you learned that you were to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That notification about the exchange on the 3rd of September did not come as a surprise, because I was waiting for it by that time. But on the 2nd of September, or perhaps in the last 15 days prior to that, that is, from the end of August into early September, deportations continued of the remaining family members of detainees, men who had left some family members behind at home. If the person who took that particular man away saw at the time that there were other family members inside that home, would remember that, and these people would be later taken to Zasavica. So I was waiting for them to come for me too, and I had already prepared for that. I had my bags packed and ready to be taken away to Zasavica. On the 2nd of September, it was a warm day. I was in my back yard together with my neighbour with whom I shared that house, and there were two more neighbours from the same street with us, all women. Since we had been without electricity for a long time by that, we cooked outdoors. And at one point, I noticed a truck was pulling up, a truck with orange tarpaulin, and I could hear somehow that below the tarpaulin, the truck was not empty, there were people inside, and you could hear the hum of their voices. And I realised at that moment that I was in danger of being taken away in this raid and deported. My children were playing with the neighbour's children at the time not far away, and my first thought was, My children are safe. I told my neighbours, "If somebody comes looking for me, tell the them I went to the Red Cross office to talk about some exchange." And perhaps naively I hid behind the garage. All I could see from then on was a policeman entering my house. I couldn't exactly see him entering the house, but I could see him climbing the stairs leading up to my door. So from my hiding place, I could see him walking about -- walking to and fro on the balcony looking for me. And failing to find me, he asked -- he asked my neighbours about me, and they replied I wasn't at home. He did not insist nor did he bother them any more with the questions. They later said that they were under the impression that he was in a hurry. He just went back to his truck, started it, and left. That happened in the afternoon of the 2nd September. And the next -- and I thought that I was safe for that day. However, I was afraid that there would be another attempt to collect me, and I went the next day to the Red Cross office to ask Mr. Tadic if any exchanges were planned. And I told him they had been to look for me already, and if no exchange materialised in the near future, I would be taken to Zasavica for certain. It was then that he told me that an exchange would be taking place the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he tell you at that time that you were going to be part of it or just simply that there was an exchange taking place?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that I would be part of it and that my husband would be included too.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it's coming to 6.00. And while there are a lot of questions, I think, that arise out of that answer, it may be wise to pick that up tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one very short question. And it can have, I think, a yes-or-no answer. And that is: To be on the exchange list, did any person ask you for money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nobody asked me for money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will adjourn and continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 14.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what happened with this original. I'm confused. Did I already have it with me, or is it somewhere around?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There's no need to worry. I have it, and I'll retain it and ensure it gets back to you when you've finished your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The document is in safe hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: at 6.00, to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of February, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
